extracted.intended_audience: readers of 19th-century philosophical/literary prose (students, scholars, general readers of Carlyle)
extracted.subtask_description: A close-reading / extraction task on an excerpt from a 19th-century philosophical novel (Sartor Resartus style), containing aphorisms and prescriptions about books, government, war, spiritual growth, and happiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of a true Book
rubrics_metrics.description: In which third truly, the last invented, lies a worth far surpassing that of the two others. Wondrous indeed is the virtue of a true Book. ... it stands from year to year, and from age to age ... and yearly comes its new produce of leaves ... every one of which is talismanic and thaumaturgic, for it can persuade men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books are likened to a 'spiritual tree' that outlasts stone cities and tilled fields; a true book's merit lies in longevity, ongoing generative commentary, and persuasive moral/spiritual influence. The passage insists one who can write such a book is as great as a city-builder or conqueror (but in a higher sense).

rubrics_metrics.name: Where skill and knowledge reside
rubrics_metrics.description: Visible Ploughmen and Hammermen there have been ... but where does your accumulated Agricultural, Metallurgic, and other Manufacturing SKILL lie warehoused? It transmits itself on the atmospheric air, on the sun's rays (by Hearing and by Vision); it is a thing aeriform, impalpable, of quite spiritual sort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge/skill cannot be 'warehoused' in buildings or objects; assess skill by its transmission (teaching, imitation, sight/hearing) rather than by physical repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government is to be judged by works, not edifices
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask me not, Where are the LAWS; where is the GOVERNMENT? ... thou findest nothing there but brick or stone houses, and some bundles of Papers tied with tape. Where, then, is that same cunningly devised almighty GOVERNMENT of theirs to be laid hands on? Everywhere, yet nowhere: seen only in its works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government is 'aeriform' and must be understood through its effects and actions rather than through inspection of palaces or paper; evaluation should focus on observable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: War as wasteful destruction of human capital
rubrics_metrics.description: From these, by certain 'Natural Enemies' of the French, there are successively selected ... thirty able-bodied men ... shipped away ... and now to that same spot ... Thirty stands fronting Thirty ... they blow the souls out of one another; and in place of sixty brisk useful craftsmen, the world has sixty dead carcasses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluating war: consider the economic and social waste—loss of skilled workers raised by communities—rather than glorified political aims; this passage frames war as a gratuitous, governmental quarrel that kills productive lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature's restorative role after human violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Nevertheless, Nature is at work; neither shall these Powder-Devilkins with their utmost devilry gainsay her: but all that gore and carnage will be shrouded in, absorbed into manure; and next year the Marchfeld will be green, nay greener.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite human destruction, assess long-term outcomes with attention to natural recuperation and renewal; nature transforms devastation into life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological equalization (use of gunpowder)
rubrics_metrics.description: Such I hold to be the genuine use of Gunpowder: that it makes all men alike tall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technology can level physical inequalities—when evaluating social effects of inventions, note their potential to democratize power or render brute strength less decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: The absurdity of duels
rubrics_metrics.description: Two little visual Spectra of men ... make pause at the distance of twelve paces asunder; whirl round; and, simultaneously by the cunningest mechanism, explode one another into Dissolution; and off-hand become Air, and Non-extant! Deuce on it (_verdammt_), the little spitfires!--Nay, I think with old Hugo von Trimberg: 'God must needs laugh outright, could such a thing be, to see his wondrous Manikins here below.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duels are to be judged as irrational, comical, and contemptible displays rather than noble acts; moral evaluation should expose their vanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wilderness temptation as necessary spiritual trial
rubrics_metrics.description: To me nothing seems more natural than that the Son of Man, when such God-given mandate first prophetically stirs within him, ... should be carried of the spirit into grim Solitudes, and there fronting the Tempter do grimmest battle ... To such Temptation are we all called.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spiritual/ethical development should be evaluated in light of trials of solitude and temptation: such ordeals are portrayed as necessary preparatory crucibles for moral progress or apostolic vocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renunciation as the beginning of true life
rubrics_metrics.description: Well did the Wisest of our time write: 'It is only with Renunciation (_Entsagen_) that Life, properly speaking, can be said to begin.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text proposes renunciation (lessening desires/claims) as a criterion for maturity; practical guidance includes reducing one's 'denominator' of wants to increase the value of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher aim than happiness: blessedness through self‑annihilation
rubrics_metrics.description: there is in man a HIGHER than Love of Happiness: he can do without Happiness, and instead thereof find Blessedness! ... By benignant fever-paroxysms is Life rooting out the deep-seated chronic Disease...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess moral/spiritual health by capacity to transcend pursuit of personal happiness and attain a state of blessedness through suffering, renunciation, or higher vocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert conviction into conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Conviction, were it never so excellent, is worthless till it convert itself into Conduct. Nay properly Conviction is not possible till then; inasmuch as all Speculation is by nature endless ... only by a felt indubitable certainty of Experience does it find any centre to revolve round, and so fashion itself into a system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard of truth or value is practical enactment and experience: intellectual belief must be tested and embodied in action to count for anything.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compassionate, brotherly stance toward mankind
rubrics_metrics.description: With an infinite Love, an infinite Pity. Poor, wandering, wayward man! ... and even for his sufferings and his sins, I now first named him Brother.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral evaluation should privilege pity and solidarity; a valid ethical vision treats fellow humans as brothers to be sheltered and comforted rather than merely judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor partial inspiration over doctrinal vengeance
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither shall ye tear out one another's eyes, struggling over 'Plenary Inspiration,' and such like: try rather to get a little even Partial Inspiration, each of you for himself. One BIBLE I know, of whose Plenary Inspiration doubt is not so much as possible; nay with my own eyes I saw the God's-Hand writing it: thereof all other Bibles are but Leaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dogmatic fights over absolute doctrinal claims; value partial, personal inspiration and a practical, lived faith. The passage counsels moderation and experiential humility in religious judgment.
